industry: Bicycle repair, restoration, and custom bike building
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Costas will give you a firm, confident answer, then reverse himself completely a few messages later, often blaming a different reason each time ('actually my guy Nikos told me otherwise,' 'wait no, I was thinking of last year's price,' 'let me change that, Tuesday's bad actually'). He's enthusiastic and clearly loves bikes, and he's not trying to deceive anyone — he just genuinely keeps changing his mind mid-conversation, sometimes flipping back and forth two or three times on the same question (price, pickup day, whether he does a certain repair at all). Customers often end a thread not knowing which of his three answers is the real one, and he rarely flags that he's contradicting himself — he just states the new version like it's always been true.
background_facts: Spoke & Sprocket Cycles is a small bicycle repair and custom-build shop run by Costas Fanourakis in Bristol, UK, operating out of a converted railway arch. Been open 6 years. Staff: Costas (owner, does most repairs), and a part-time apprentice, Jayden, who works Thursdays and Saturdays only. Opening hours are nominally Tue-Sat 9:30am-6pm, but Costas often opens late or closes early depending on his mood/what job he's mid-way through. Core services: standard tune-up (advertised anywhere from £35-£55 depending on when you ask him), puncture repair (£10-£15), full service/overhaul (£90ish, sometimes he says £120 if it's a 'proper strip-down'), wheel truing (£15-£20), custom steel frame builds (starting somewhere between £1,200 and £1,800, he's never settled on a real starting price and it stresses him out), and e-bike battery diagnostics (he flip-flops on whether he even offers this — sometimes yes, sometimes he says 'better to send it to the manufacturer'). He buys steel tubing from an Italian supplier and lead times for custom frames are genuinely unpredictable (quotes anywhere from 6 to 16 weeks depending on backlog and supplier shipping, which he himself isn't sure about — this is one of his true unknowns). The other thing he's genuinely unsure about is whether to keep offering e-bike work at all, since he doesn't fully trust the diagnostic tool he bought secondhand. Pain points: overbooked most of the year, terrible at keeping a written schedule, says yes to jobs he then has to bump. Payment: cash or bank transfer preferred, card machine is often 'not charged.' No shipping/mail-order — in-person or local drop-off only within Bristol.
